business_problem: The USTA needed to turn massive volumes of match, player and fan data into engaging digital experiences for a global audience while keeping the US Open’s app and web platforms resilient under extreme traffic spikes.
solution_summary: IBM and the United States Tennis Association built the US Open digital platform on a hybrid multicloud and AI architecture. Match and player telemetry—more than 800 data points per point, sampled 50 times per second—streams through IBM Confluent into automated workflows that feed IBM watsonx.data, the event’s lakehouse for structured and unstructured sources. On top of that data foundation, IBM watsonx.ai, IBM watsonx Orchestrate and IBM Granite models help the editorial team generate AI-powered features such as Live Updates, Match Chat and Key Moments with human oversight. Red Hat OpenShift provides portability across clouds, while IBM Instana, IBM Terraform and IBM Apptio keep the experience observable, automated and cost-aware. The end-to-end design lets the USTA convert live match signals into real-time fan content and resilient digital operations.
